_doc: Codex Rites page: a hint shows once its quest is done (the quest completes when the step opens). Text equals the in-game clue (lang ritual.*).

hints.text: The altar eats before it fights. Set one feast upon the stone, a dish worth a guest-gift.
The hollow king shed his crown among the bones of the old herd. Lay sixteen at the foot of the stone.
The dead of the wood walk his old trail. Let twenty fall in sight of the altar.
Nine trees stand in the stone's mind. Seal them in this order, no other: the door-wood, the strong one; then the one that bleeds when it is cut; then red berries set against the witch.
The stone will answer only when the moon stands highest over the stone. Use the altar then.
Whatever you woke will come to see who woke it. Hold the altar for 60 breaths of the sun-count and do not leave it.
The altar eats before it fights. Set one feast upon the stone, a dish worth a guest-gift.
What boils in the heart must first be fed. Sixteen red-bark warts for the pot.
Eight-legged cooks stir the lower dark. Twenty of them must be unmade.

Nine trees stand in the stone's mind. Seal them in this order, no other: the door-wood, the strong one; then the pale one that wears the first white; then the winter king, green when all is grey; then the one that bleeds when it is cut.

Whatever you woke will come to see who woke it. Hold the altar for 60 breaths of the sun-count and do not leave it.

The drowned reaver's coat is made of sea-glass. Twenty-four shards, and no fewer.
The sea gives back its dead on the shore. Fifteen must go back to it.

Nine trees stand in the stone's mind. Seal them in this order, no other: kin of the tree that holds up the world; then the nut of the one who knows; then the one that bleeds when it is cut; then the nut of the one who knows.
The stone will answer only as the sun drowns and the first stars wake. Use the altar then.
Whatever you woke will come to see who woke it. Hold the altar for 75 breaths of the sun-count and do not leave it.
The altar eats before it fights. Set one feast upon the stone, a dish worth a guest-gift.
The Sovereign's hearth wants iron by the block: eight, cold and square.
Bones that never rusted still march in his smoke. Thirty is the count.

Nine trees stand in the stone's mind. Seal them in this order, no other: the weeper by the water; then the nut of the one who knows; then kin of the tree that holds up the world; then the winter king, green when all is grey; then red berries set against the witch.

The weaver spins in the dark of what you carry. Sixty-four threads for her loom.
Her children cover the old roads. Thirty of them fewer.

The sun-dried dead keep its old watch. Twenty-five must be put to rest.

The sleepless sky-things are its scouts. Ten must fall.

Axe-bearers cleared the grove that bore it. Fifteen must answer.

The Wheel is wound by small wheels. Twelve clocks, wound and ticking.
Those who step between moments are its spokes. Twenty spokes must break.
